title: Michael Kratsios ethics completion and recusal ledger — bounded records result
summary: The nominee record establishes divestment and recusal commitments, but the authoritative compliance, completion, recusal and waiver records were not recovered from indexed public pages.

sources.title: Nomination of Michael Kratsios — Senate hearing record
Ethics Agreements:Where Ethics Obligations Become Action
OGE Form 201:Request an Individual’s Ethics Documents

data.question: Did Michael Kratsios complete the divestments and recusals promised in his 2025 ethics agreement, on what dates, and were any waivers, authorizations or extensions issued?
data.method: Reconcile Senate nominee records with OGE rules and current public disclosure surfaces; search indexed official surfaces for post-confirmation ethics documents.
data.framework: Commitment, deadline, completion evidence, recusal evidence and waiver evidence remain separate. Missing records are not evidence of non-compliance.
findings: The Senate questionnaire says Kratsios would divest Scale AI equity/options, bitcoin and ethereum if confirmed and follow ethics-agreement recusals.
The Senate confirmed Kratsios on March 25, 2025.

OGE says PAS appointees ordinarily complete ethics-agreement actions and file a Certification of Ethics Agreement Compliance within 90 days of confirmation unless another deadline or extension applies; the ordinary 90-day point was June 23, 2025.
The current public disclosure interface shows the pre-service Scale AI and cryptocurrency holdings and later public-market transactions but does not itself establish the required disposition dates.

A bounded indexed-web search did not recover Kratsios's signed ethics agreement, compliance certification, certificate of divestiture, extension/modification, recusal memorandum, authorization or waiver.
conclusions: The indexed public record supports the commitments but not a dated completion ledger.
The mission is blocked on authoritative public-document acquisition, not completed and not evidence of non-compliance.
recommendations: Obtain the signed ethics agreement, compliance certification, amendments/extensions, divestiture certificates and public waivers/recusal records through OGE/OSTP's authorized public-access route.
counterarguments: An absent transaction in an aggregator is not proof that a required disposition did not occur.
Former-employer retirement accounts without further employer contributions are not continuing employment.
limitations: The OGE individual-disclosures collection requires an interactive requester flow that the research agent cannot complete by inventing requester information.

workflow.next_action: Acquire authoritative ethics documents through OGE/OSTP, then reopen.
